notes: Performance evidence requires source-granted operation permissions and an explicit operation hash/key ID. A resend cannot add or change evidence; the first authenticated producer is retained. Plugin calls without an operation reference remain unassigned. Unknown package releases are never replaced by the latest package.
Location is an annotation: a resent event retains its first stored actor.location even when a later lookup differs. Other event facts must match.
What the Argus collector takes and how its engine reads a marker. Written by apps/api/test/sdk-contract.test.ts in argus.

ingestRequest is the body of POST /ingest/events; browserCall is the body of POST /ingest/browser; browserPayloadCall is the body of POST /ingest/browser/payloads, one WebMCP tool run with the content its page captured, sent as JSON text while the page is open (at most 16 MiB; a payload is truncated only when it cannot fit, its truncated flag set).

A WebMCP tool run (kind agent.tool.executed) carries webmcp: the tool name (null where it does not match http.tool's pattern), how it ended (answered, threw, or is_error for a result that said it failed), and the JSON size of its arguments and result. Never their content, except in browserPayloadCall.

The schemas are what the collector stores. It does not refuse a call for a field they do not name: it removes the field, stores none of it and counts it on the call. Anything else they do not allow, a new value of a field they name included, refuses the call.

The collector also refuses what these schemas cannot say: an event timed more than 30 days before its call arrives, or more than a day after; an event carrying a hashed address, principal or registration in a call whose component names no hashKeyId; a fingerprint naming more than 64 components, or with a component nested more than 32 levels deep; and a string or field name anywhere in a body holding a NUL (U+0000) or half a surrogate pair.
markers.parsed is the engine reading each raw value as an agent sent it back: case ignored, "-" dropped, I and L read as 1 and O as 0.

body.stringValue: Synthetic message not selected for export.

mcpSpans.name: Transport span: mcp.<method>, or mcp.<method>:<name> for tools/call, resources/read and prompts/get (the tool, the requested resource URI, the prompt), at most 256 UTF-16 units; with no name, mcp.<method> and no colon. Handler span: mcp.<method>:<the name the tool, resource or prompt was registered under>.
mcpSpans.transport: One span per JSON-RPC message the server received, set as a step (agentrail.step true, agentrail.step.surface mcp, agentrail.step.kind tool.call for tools/call and mcp.<method> otherwise), with layer transport. client.name, client.version and protocol.version are what that message carried (its _meta, the mcp-protocol-version header, or for initialize its params), never a negotiated value. ERROR status for a JSON-RPC error answer, whatever raised it (jsonrpc.error_code set to the code on the wire), a tool result with isError (result.is_error true), or a request the transport refused with an HTTP status of 400 or more and no JSON-RPC answer.
mcpSpans.errorTypes: error.type on an ERROR span: McpJsonRpcError for a JSON-RPC error answer, McpOperationError for a tool result with isError, McpTransportRejected for a request refused with no JSON-RPC answer, otherwise the thrown error's own type name.
mcpSpans.handler: A tool, resource or prompt callback inside a transport span: its child, layer handler, and no step (no agentrail.step). Alone, as an SDK without the transport wrapper sends it, it is the step itself and carries what a transport span would where the callback can see it: client name, version and protocol, session.id_hash, and result.is_error for a tools/call result with isError.
mcpSpans.sizes: request.bytes and response.bytes are the UTF-8 length of the JSON-RPC message as the SDK encodes it, without whitespace.
mcpSpans.session: session.id_hash is the keyed hash (the resource hash key, as principal ids are hashed) of the Mcp-Session-Id the server issued, never an id only a request carried; absent where the server issued none (stateless HTTP, stdio, the 2026-07-28 protocol). It needs agentrail.hash_key_id on the resource.
mcpSpans.payloads: request.payload (the request params) and response.payload (the result, or the error object) are sent only when the application turns payload capture on, which needs a redact hook, as JSON text after it; a hook that drops the payload sends neither, and one that fails or returns what is not JSON is the loss code payload_redact_failed. A request with no answer (a notification, a cancelled request) still sends its request payload. No length of ours bounds them, except that a span's two payloads together are cut to limits.mcpPayloadBytes (UTF-8, on a character boundary), the longer first, with its truncated flag set, so one span always fits an export. An SDK holds at most 64 MiB of payload text per queue (loss code payload_budget). The collector keeps them only for a source whose Admin turned payload capture on.
